sub_topics.description: Let begin with O of 1 constant time. Anything that has a runtime complexity of O of 1 will take the same amount of time regardless of the data size. A few examples would include the random access of an element within an array and inserting at the beginning of a linked list. So O of 1 is extremely fast. sub_topics.name: Other types of Big O notation
sub_topics.description: O is also known as linear time. As the amount of data increases, the time it takes to complete something will increase proportionally linearly. That would include looping through the elements in an array and searching through a linked list. Next we have O of N log N, also known as quasi-linear time. This would include a quick sort, merge sort, and heap sort. We'll talk about these concepts in future videos. So for the most part, this is very similar to linear time. Then we have O of n squared, also known as quadratic time. A few examples would include insertion sort, selection sort, and bubble sort.
